questions.question: Describe the mechanism of nucleophilic addition to a carbonyl group and explain why aldehydes are more reactive than ketones.
questions.solution:
The carbonyl carbon is electron-deficient (sp², δ⁺) and the π bond is polarised, so nucleophiles attack the carbon:

(i) Nu⁻ attacks the carbon, the π electrons move to oxygen giving a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate; (ii) protonation of the alkoxide by the medium completes the addition, giving an alcohol (or a derivative if the nucleophile is followed by loss of water).

**Aldehydes vs ketones:** two alkyl groups in a ketone release electron density by +I effect, reducing the carbon's δ⁺, and their bulk also hinders attack. Hence aldehydes react faster; formaldehyde is the most reactive.
questions.knowledgeNote: Acid catalysis helps weak nucleophiles (protonation increases electrophilicity); base catalysis helps strong ones — the intermediate is stabilised.

questions.question: What is the aldol condensation? Write the reaction of acetaldehyde with dilute NaOH and state the product.
questions.solution:
**Aldol condensation:** an aldehyde or ketone with at least one α-hydrogen forms a carbanion (enolate) in dilute base; this attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule, giving a β-hydroxy aldehyde (aldol). On heating, aldol loses water to give an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl.

For acetaldehyde: CH₃CHO + CH₃CHO → **CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO (aldol)** → on heating, **CH₃CH=CHCHO (crotonaldehyde)**.
questions.knowledgeNote: No α-hydrogen → no aldol: benzaldehyde (no α-H) instead undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH, giving benzyl alcohol and benzoate.

questions.question: How will you distinguish between (a) an aldehyde and a ketone, (b) acetaldehyde and benzaldehyde, (c) a carboxylic acid and a phenol?
questions.solution:
**(a)** Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror and Fehling's solution a red-brown Cu₂O precipitate with aldehydes only; ketones do not respond.

**(b)** Iodoform test — acetaldehyde (CH₃CO− group) gives a yellow precipitate of CHI₃ with I₂/NaOH; benzaldehyde does not.

**(c)** Carboxylic acids liberate CO₂ from NaHCO₃ with brisk effervescence; phenols do not (phenol dissolves only in NaOH).
questions.knowledgeNote: The iodoform test detects the CH₃CO− group or a CH₃CH(OH)− group, so it also identifies ethanol and methyl ketones.
